title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: HubSpot connector in the Researcher agent
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing and connector controls are supported. The corrected staged-rollout path matches Microsoft Learn, and the enable/disable label appears in the HubSpot screenshot description. Earlier preview defaults are clearly distinguished from current documentation.

claims.claim: The HubSpot connector lets Researcher use third-party HubSpot information to enrich generated responses.
claims.quote: The HubSpot connector allows users using the Researcher agent to be able to leverage 3rd party information from HubSpot to enrich generated responses with relevant information.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Federated connector access uses the user's identity and source-system permissions.
claims.quote: The authenticated user's identity and permissions in the source system govern tool access. Users can only access information they're authorized to view and change data they're authorized to modify.

claims.quote: Users can discover the data source in the Sources menu in the Researcher agent, in deep research mode in Microsoft 365 Copilot chat, and in Copilot Chat where available.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Users authenticate to connector data sources with their own credentials when prompted.
claims.quote: Users authenticate by using their own credentials when prompted to connect to the data sources.

claims.claim: Researcher does not support write, update or delete actions, so its federated connectors remain read-only.
claims.quote: The Researcher agent doesn't support write, update, or delete actions. Federated Copilot connectors remain read-only in this experience.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot release notes include this item under November 4, 2026.
claims.quote:
## November 4, 2026
### Microsoft 365 Copilot extensibility
1. **User can use HubSpot Connector in Researcher** [Web]

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: HubSpot information is retrieved into Copilot responses rather than remaining solely inside HubSpot.
claims.quote: Copilot selects relevant connector tools at runtime and uses the live results returned by the source to respond in the conversation.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Earlier early-access preview documentation described federated connectors as enabled by default for a tenant.
claims.quote:
# Federated Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors overview (early access preview)
## Admin experience and controls
Federated connectors are enabled by default for a tenant.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Earlier preview documentation gave Microsoft-published connectors a seven-calendar-day admin-only review window before user availability.
claims.quote: When a Microsoft-published federated connector first appears in the admin center, it's available only to admins for seven calendar days before it's available to users.

claims.claim: Earlier preview documentation listed HubSpot among Microsoft-published federated connectors.
claims.quote:
## Microsoft-published federated connectors
Microsoft provides a set of federated connectors by default. Currently, federated connectors are available for the following data sources:
1. Canva
2. HubSpot

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Current documentation describes availability through publisher-type, User access and individual connector settings.
claims.quote: Use Agent and plugin access to allow or block connectors in bulk by publisher type, User access to set which users can use connectors, and connector-level settings to enable, disable, or stage individual connectors.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Current documentation does not state an unconditional default arrival state for the HubSpot connector.
claims.quote: Searched: HubSpot federated connector default publisher specific settings pricing subscription Microsoft Learn; read current federated-connectors-overview and manage-federated-connectors. Defaults are conditional on publisher settings; current HubSpot publisher/default is not specified.

claims.claim: Microsoft-built connectors are available by default when the Microsoft publisher option is selected and the user is included in User access.
claims.quote: Microsoft-built federated connectors are available by default when you select Allow agents and plugins built by Microsoft in Agent and plugin access and include the user in User access.

claims.claim: External-publisher connectors require the external-publisher option or an admin enabling the individual connector.
claims.quote: Connectors from external publishers are available only when you select Allow agents and plugins built by external publishers, or when an admin turns on the individual connector.

claims.claim: The current gallery does not identify HubSpot's publisher type.
claims.quote: Searched: HubSpot federated connector default publisher specific settings pricing subscription Microsoft Learn. Read current federated-connectors-overview gallery and availability sections; HubSpot is listed under CRM without a publisher designation.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Connector availability settings and source-system permissions govern HubSpot access in Researcher, without an indexing mechanism.
claims.quote:
Are managed and governed by admins in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Access data using the user's identity and permissions.
Don't index external data into Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: OAuth 2.0 and encrypted communication secure federated connector access and authentication.
claims.quote: OAuth 2.0 and encrypted communication ensure secure access and authentication.

claims.claim: An MCP server that restricts incoming traffic by source IP must allow Copilot's static egress IP addresses.
claims.quote: If your MCP server restricts incoming traffic by source IP address, configure its firewall to allow the static egress IP addresses used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: Write, update and delete tools belong to the connector and are not enabled separately.
claims.quote: Write, update, and delete tools are part of the connector and aren't enabled separately.

claims.claim: The connector tool-list admin view is marked Coming soon and is not available for all connectors.
claims.quote:
### View a connector's tools in the admin center (Coming soon)
Viewing tools in the admin center isn't available for all connectors.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Current overview and management documentation do not repeat the seven-day admin review window.
claims.quote: Searched: federated connectors HubSpot preview seven Microsoft default. Read current federated-connectors-overview and manage-federated-connectors in full; the seven-calendar-day passage appears only in early-access preview search excerpts.

claims.claim: A connector's publisher type must be allowed, or the individual connector must be turned on, for user visibility.
claims.quote:
A user sees a federated connector in Copilot only when all of the following are true:
The connector's publisher type is allowed in Agent and plugin access, or an admin turned on the connector individually.

claims.claim: A connector must be enabled for user visibility.
claims.quote:
A user sees a federated connector in Copilot only when all of the following are true:
The connector is enabled.

claims.claim: User visibility requires membership in the User access population.
claims.quote:
A user sees a federated connector in Copilot only when all of the following are true:
The user is included in User access.

claims.claim: User visibility requires inclusion in the connector's staged rollout.
claims.quote:
A user sees a federated connector in Copilot only when all of the following are true:
The user is included in the connector's staged rollout.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; summary; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Federated connectors are available to tenants and users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence or Microsoft 365 E7.
claims.quote: Federated Copilot connectors are available only to tenants and users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license (or Microsoft 365 E7).

claims.claim: Copilot Studio licences and Microsoft 365 Copilot pay-as-you-go do not support federated connectors.
claims.quote: They aren't supported with Copilot Studio licenses or Microsoft 365 Copilot pay-as-you-go.

claims.claim: The prerequisites list a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence for every user querying a federated source.
claims.quote: A Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license for every user who queries the federated source. For an eligibility matrix, see Licensing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Connector grounding in Copilot is included for organisations with Microsoft 365 Copilot licences.
claims.quote: If your organization has Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, connector grounding in Copilot is included, and no extra charges apply.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No extra charges apply to connector grounding for organisations with Microsoft 365 Copilot licences.
claims.quote: If your organization has Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, connector grounding in Copilot is included, and no extra charges apply.

claims.claim: The Microsoft documentation does not state the cost of the HubSpot subscription itself.
claims.quote: Searched: HubSpot federated connector default publisher specific settings pricing subscription Microsoft Learn. Read prerequisites and federated-connectors-overview; these document Microsoft entitlement and grounding charges, not HubSpot subscription pricing.

claims.claim: The federated connector management page names Global Administrator or Search Administrator as required roles.
claims.quote:
To manage federated connectors, you need one of the following administrator roles:
Global Administrator
Search Administrator

claims.claim: The connector prerequisites page requires an AI administrator to configure and deploy Copilot connectors.
claims.quote: To configure and deploy Copilot connectors, you must be an AI administrator in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Admins find federated connectors in Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot connectors > Your connections.
claims.quote: Admins can manage federated Copilot connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center by choosing Copilot connectors > Your connections.

claims.claim: Users can turn off a data source in Researcher.
claims.quote: Users can disable the data source at any time by turning off the source in Researcher or by managing the source in Copilot Chat settings.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Connector setting changes can take up to 10 minutes to take effect.
claims.quote: Changes can take up to 10 minutes to take effect across Microsoft 365 experiences.

claims.claim: Connector publishers can add or change tools over time.
claims.quote: The actions available through a connector depend on the tools exposed by the connector publisher. Publishers can add or change tools over time.

claims.claim: Publisher-type availability is controlled in Microsoft 365 admin center at Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access > publisher type.
claims.quote:
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access.
Clear the publisher types you want to block:
Allow agents and plugins built by Microsoft
Allow agents and plugins built by your organization
Allow agents and plugins built by external publishers

claims.claim: Clearing a publisher type sets existing connectors of that type to No users and blocks availability of future connectors of that type.
claims.quote: When you clear an option, existing connectors of that type remain visible to admins in Copilot connectors > Your connections, but their staged rollout is set to No users. Connectors of that type released later aren't available to users.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; rendered controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Tenant User access is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access.
claims.quote: User access in Agents > Settings applies to all agents and plugins, including federated connectors delivered as Microsoft 365 app packages.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[1].note; controls[3].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: User access sets the maximum connector audience; staged rollout can narrow but cannot widen that population.
claims.quote:
Only these users can use any connector. Connector staging can narrow but not widen this population.
User access doesn't turn connectors on or off; it sets the maximum population.

claims.claim: User access offers All users as the default, Specific users or groups, and No users.
claims.quote: Options: All users (default), Specific users or groups, No users.

claims.claim: An individual connector can be enabled or disabled in Microsoft 365 admin center at Copilot connectors > Your connections > connector > Enable/disable data source.
claims.quote:
Admins can manage federated Copilot connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center by choosing Copilot connectors > Your connections.
Screenshot of the HubSpot connector in the admin center with Staged rollout and Enable/disable data source highlighted.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; controls[3].note; rendered controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Specific users or Microsoft Entra ID groups are staged through Copilot connectors > Your connections > Staged rollout > Add staging.
claims.quote:
Admins can manage federated Copilot connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center by choosing Copilot connectors > Your connections.
Limit a connector to specific users or Microsoft Entra ID groups by choosing Add staging in the Staged rollout column.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents tool-level and connector-level blocking at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools.
claims.quote: | Tools block / unblock | Agents > Tools | Tool-level and connector-level blocking. |

claims.where: controls[0].api; controls[1].api; controls[2].api; controls[3].api; controls[4].api; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API or automation equivalent for these publisher, User access, enable/disable, staged-rollout and blocking settings at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph federated connectors admin publisher Agent plugin access User access staged rollout enable disable tools block API PowerShell. Read federated-connectors-overview, manage-federated-connectors and set-up-custom-federated-connectors FAQ excerpts; no matching automation found.

claims.claim: An individual connector setting takes precedence over bulk Agent and plugin access, while User access always applies.
claims.quote: A setting you make on an individual connector takes precedence over the bulk Agent and plugin access setting. User access always applies.

claims.claim: Individual connectors can be made available from Your connections even when the publisher type is cleared.
claims.quote: To make a specific connector available, open it in Your connections and set its staged rollout to the users or groups you want.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no additional setting specific to HubSpot beyond the listed connector controls.
claims.quote: Searched: HubSpot federated connector default publisher specific settings pricing subscription Microsoft Learn. Read federated-connectors-overview, HubSpot pane description and manage-federated-connectors; no additional HubSpot-specific setting was documented.

claims.claim: The overview names Microsoft Purview for connector activity auditing without giving an audit navigation path.
claims.quote: Can read data and, where a connector provides the tools, create, update, or delete data with the user's approval. Admins can audit activity in Microsoft Purview.
